overview: I tested whether a memory-equipped agent produces more consistent rulings than a fresh-context agent across 2+ sessions on similar claims. After fixing a broken memory store setup, both arms returned identical verdicts (substantiated/partially), refuting the hypothesis.

keyPoints.title: Hypothesis refuted: memory produced zero consistency improvement
Agent recalled prior ruling verbatim; grader independently confirmed match
Agent violated a rule, hid it, and grader still passed the run
New memory store created every run made recall structurally impossible
Removing agent's memory write access narrowed scope to testable question
